small_guidance:
- The conv (nn.Conv3d) now dominates runtime since the post-conv fusion is already a single-pass kernel; further tuning of the post-conv kernel has limited headroom. For the existing kernel, try BLOCK_S=1024 with num_warps=8, and/or persistent storage of x in registers between pass1 and pass2 by making BLOCK_S large enough that n_blocks==1 (S=14×30×30=12600 — too large, so two-pass remains necessary). Sweep BLOCK_S∈{256,512,1024,2048} × num_warps∈{4,8} via triton.autotune keyed on (C,S).
- Fold the conv bias and the first multiplier into a fused conv epilogue (bias_eff = bias*mult) so pass1 only does (x+bias_eff) instead of x*mult — saves one mul per element and lets the kernel ingest raw conv output.
- Pre-scale and pre-square the multiplier on host (m, m*m) and pass both, so sumsq accumulation can use x*x*m2 directly without recomputing y=x*m twice.
large_guidance:
- The torch nn.Conv3d is the dominant cost (fast_p≈0.54 with the tail already fused). Replace it with a custom Triton conv3d implemented as implicit-im2col GEMM: one program per (N, OC tile, output-spatial tile), gathering input with computed offsets, with a small kernel volume (3×3×3=27) that fits well in the K-loop. Fuse the conv epilogue with `*multiplier` and pass the result directly into the existing instance-norm/clamp/max kernel, avoiding a write+read of the [N,16,14,30,30] tensor.
- Even better: fuse conv+multiplier+InstanceNorm pass1 (sum/sumsq accumulation) into a single program-per-(N,C) kernel that streams output spatial tiles, since InstanceNorm reduces over S per (N,C). This collapses three kernel launches into one and keeps the post-conv tensor in registers/SMEM.
- Use channels_last_3d (NDHWC) for the conv output so the channel-max reduction at the end has C contiguous, allowing a single-load reduction over a 16-wide vector per spatial element.
